'Has successor' is functional..why: The successor of a whole number n is n + 1, one number; Wikipedia's Peano axioms article calls the successor a single-valued function. Everyone learns 'the next number' as one number.

notes: RBox contraction (functional) paired with mathematics-replace-0018: removes the functionality of 'has successor'. The record says 'whole number' throughout because in a partial order an element can have several immediate successors. Instances use letters (p, q, r; m, n, k), as the revision does, since with particular numbers the conclusions follow by arithmetic. The first instance asks whether the two successors could differ (no before), the second whether they must be equal (yes). The direct question asks the possibility the removal opens (no); prompt_subject is 'successors', the question's wording of the relation. Side facts about hexagons are copied from the revision. Unrelated near asks about another function-like quantity (absolute value, no). Caveat: the successor of n is n + 1 by definition, so uniqueness is the definition itself and a model may keep it. hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1).
